questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the maximum air leakage during a static test is ____ per minute.
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test on a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, air should not leak faster than 5 psi per minute. If it does, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs to be repaired.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that moves air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes when used
A part inside the braking unit that lets air move freely

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device in an air brake system. It drops a mechanical arm into your view when air pressure drops below 60 psi.

questions.question: When driving:

options.text: Always drive at the posted speed limit.
Always drive slightly below the posted speed limit.
Adjust your speed based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your speed based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast causes many fatal crashes. Always adjust your speed to match the road and traffic conditions around you.

questions.question: Use at least ____ to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo, even small items, must be held down with a minimum of two tie-downs.

questions.question: Before a trip, inspect your windshield. Do all of the following except:

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the windshield wipers for proper spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: Check for cracks or problems on your windshield that might block your view. Check the wiper arms for proper spring tension. Check the wiper blades for damage, stiff rubber, and proper attachment.

questions.question: When driving down a steep grade, your brakes may fade. What happens when brakes fade?

options.text: They work differently from front to back.

questions.explanation: Using brakes too much on a steep downgrade causes them to overheat and work poorly. To prevent this, use engine braking on steep hills instead of relying only on your brakes.

questions.question: Eating while driving is:

options.text: A good way to save time.
Acceptable if you eat foods that are easy to eat.

questions.explanation: Smoking, eating, or drinking while driving are distracting and dangerous. Plan ahead and stop to eat during long trips instead of eating while you drive.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: How quickly you arrive at your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner scores you on your driving maneuvers and your general driving behavior during the on-road test.

questions.question: Bridges usually:

options.text: Freeze only when the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
Freeze after other road surfaces freeze.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road. Be extra careful when crossing bridges if the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: A fatigued driver:

options.text: Is usually more careful than a typical driver.
May be slower to make critical decisions than a typical driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be slower to make critical decisions than a typical driver.
questions.explanation: Fatigued drivers are slower to see or react to hazards. Drowsy drivers have trouble making critical decisions quickly.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the roadway:

options.text: May hide a heavy object that could damage your vehicle.
Should be avoided by leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: May hide a heavy object that could damage your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is dangerous. A cardboard box or paper bag that looks harmless may contain something hard or heavy inside. This could seriously damage your vehicle.

questions.question: Which of these is okay to find during a pre-trip tire inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread of 2/32 of an inch deep

questions.explanation: When checking your tires, make sure front tires have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. All tires must be the same size, not cracked, have proper air pressure, and be in good condition.

questions.question: What keeps wheels from locking up when you brake?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking up when you apply the brakes.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. On equipped vehicles, you control it with a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: Regrooved tires are:

options.text: Allowed only on the front of a bus.
Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
Not allowed anywhere on a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
questions.explanation: You cannot use regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires on the front of a bus. You can only use them on the rear.

questions.question: If you drive a truck that needs a CDL:

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You only need a seat belt if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You only need a seat belt when driving a tank trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: For safety, you must wear your seat belt at all times when operating a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: When driving with covered cargo, a flapping cover:
questions.explanation: Cargo covers should not flap. They can tear off and uncover your cargo. Loose covers can also block other drivers' views.

questions.question: What is the best advice for driving in fog?

options.text: Avoid driving in fog if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving in fog if possible.
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is dangerous. Avoid it if you can. If you must drive in fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: Poor weight balance in a trailer:
questions.explanation: Poor weight balance in a trailer makes handling unsafe. Too much or too little weight on the front axle makes steering difficult. Weight should be spread evenly from front to back and side to side, and as low as possible.

questions.question: Which of these crimes would NOT disqualify someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: Certain crimes will disqualify you from getting a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. These include kidnapping, smuggling, and immigration violations. More serious crimes like murder can result in a lifetime ban.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a header board?

options.text: Protect drivers from being hit by cargo.
Protect drivers' heads when entering the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect drivers from being hit by cargo.
questions.explanation: A header board protects a driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: What color is the ABS malfunction lamp?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow malfunction lamps.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems add alcohol to the system?

options.text: To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
To prevent people from breathing the air from the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to help prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: What does ABS do?

options.text: Prevent the air compressor from overheating
Prevent front brakes from working on ice
Prevent braking when downshifting would be better

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) keeps wheels from locking up when you brake hard, especially on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What should be true about the drive shaft?

options.text: It should be bent toward the passenger side.
It should be bent toward the driver's side.
It should be bent to one side or the other.

questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, check that the drive shaft is not bent or cracked.

questions.question: A vehicle with ABS uses a ____ light to show that the system is not working properly.
questions.explanation: ABS malfunction lamps are usually yellow. If the ABS isn't working, you can still use the vehicle's regular brakes.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in an air brake system, it activates an electric switch that:

options.text: Turns on the low pressure warning light.
Turns off the low pressure warning light.

questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure moves an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: How do you use the controlled braking method?

options.text: Apply brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means applying the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep your steering movements very small when using this method.

questions.question: What should you do if the road is covered in fog?
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is always dangerous. If possible, don't drive when there is fog.

questions.question: What is a good way to reduce stress while driving?
questions.explanation: Stress can cause aggressive driving, which is dangerous. Calming music helps you relax while driving.

questions.question: When making tight turns, what should a driver do?

options.text: Open the door for a better look.

questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight turns.

questions.question: What does tire load mean?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a certain pressure.

questions.question: How often must drivers check that cargo is secure?
questions.explanation: Check cargo security within the first 50 miles of a trip. Then check again every three hours or every 150 miles.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of dry bulk tanks?

options.text: They usually have low centers of gravity.
They usually have high centers of gravity.
They usually are not allowed to cross railroad tracks.
They cannot be driven on interstates.

questions.correctAnswerText: They usually have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity and need careful driving. The materials inside can shift during travel, which changes how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: What is the most common type of foundation brake?
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: What is blocking used for?

options.text: Prevent cargo from being loaded too high.
Prevent cargo from being unloaded too quickly.

questions.explanation: Blocking is placed in front, behind, and on the sides of cargo to stop it from sliding while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: If your brakes fail on a downhill slope, what should you do?

options.text: Let the vehicle slow down on its own.

questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill slope, an escape ramp is the safest way to stop your vehicle.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: How many alcoholic drinks were consumed
How fast the drinks were consumed

questions.explanation: BAC is affected by the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the person's weight. The temperature of the drinks does not affect BAC.

questions.question: When should cargo be inspected during a trip?

options.text: Only at the start of the trip.
Only after driving a long distance.

questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start driving. During the trip, check it within the first 50 miles, every three hours or 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery right after rain starts?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.
Tires are not designed to drive in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first begins. Fresh rainwater mixes with oil and grease on the road and creates a slick film. As rain continues, this mixture washes away.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, how often must you check that it is secure?
questions.explanation: Check cargo securement before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: What happens when you transport hanging meat as cargo?

options.text: It creates a safe driving situation.
It creates a low center of gravity.

questions.explanation: Hanging meat creates an unstable load. The truck may become top-heavy and swinging meat can affect steering. Use extra caution on sharp curves and highway ramps.

questions.question: What should you do if mirrors are dirty before starting a trip?

options.text: They will become clean after driving a short distance.

questions.explanation: During pre-trip inspection, check mirrors and windshield for dirt or anything that blocks your view. Clean them as needed.

questions.question: How can you increase visibility at dawn or dusk when other vehicles have trouble seeing you?
questions.explanation: At dawn or dusk, and in snow or rain, turn on your headlights. This makes it easier for other drivers to see your vehicle.

questions.question: When alley docking, how should your vehicle be parked?

options.text: With the front bumper on the front boundary line.
With the rear wheels over the rear boundary line.
Straight within the parking space boundaries.
At an angle within the parking space boundaries.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight within the parking space boundaries.
questions.explanation: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Back your vehicle straight into the alley. Park in a straight position within the space boundaries.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, where should you stand?

options.text: As close to the fire as possible.
As far away from the fire as possible.
Aim the extinguisher at the top of the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: As far away from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: Stand as far away from the fire as possible. Aim the extinguisher at the base of the fire, not the flames. If unsure which extinguisher to use, especially for hazardous materials, wait for firefighters.

questions.question: Which is not a type of tie-down equipment?
questions.explanation: Use proper tie-downs to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer. Tie-down equipment includes ropes, straps, and chains.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the brake control knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob.
questions.explanation: Newer vehicles with air brakes have a yellow diamond-shaped knob for parking brakes. Pull it out to set the parking brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: When doing a driver's side parallel parking maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Pull forward directly into the parking space.
Back up past the parking space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on your left. Back your vehicle into the space with the rear as close to the rear of the space as possible. Your vehicle must be completely within the space boundaries.
